title: One-dimensional constancy theorem: zero distributional derivative on (0, ∞) forces a.e. constancy (du Bois-Reymond; Simon 6.2.34 for n = 1)
statement: Let g : ℝ → ℝ be locally integrable on (0, ∞). Suppose that ∫_{(0,∞)} g(t)·φ'(t) dt = 0 for every C^∞ function φ : ℝ → ℝ (ContDiff of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. infinitely differentiable) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ (0, ∞), where φ' = deriv φ. Then there is a constant c ∈ ℝ with g(t) = c for almost every t ∈ (0, ∞).
lean_statement: ∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, LocallyIntegrableOn g (Ioi 0) → (∀ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ Ioi 0 → ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), g t * deriv φ t = 0) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ))), g t = c
